OpenCut: render the same timeline JSON used by the GUI editor.

The CLI uses FFmpeg; the GUI uses GStreamer. The shared timeline module owns only
format types and serialization rules. The applications own I/O and rendering.

Commands: probe, new, assemble, transcribe, validate, inspect, schema, docs, still, render.
All accept --json. Results: stdout. Progress: stderr, at most once per five seconds
plus completion. --progress none suppresses it. There is no edit command.

Workflow:
  opencut probe media.mp4 --json
  opencut new episode.timeline.json --fps 30000/1001 --json
  opencut schema --json
  opencut --project-root /project validate scenes/episode.timeline.json --json
  opencut --project-root /project inspect scenes/episode.timeline.json --json
  opencut --project-root /project still scenes/episode.timeline.json --at 50% -o preview.png
  opencut --project-root /project render scenes/episode.timeline.json -o output.mp4 --dry-run --json
  opencut --project-root /project render scenes/episode.timeline.json -o output.mp4 --progress json --json

Timeline/output arguments resolve from the working directory. Relative asset paths
resolve from --project-root, defaulting to the working directory, NOT the timeline
directory. Absolute asset paths work unchanged. Keep referenced original media.

Use opencut schema for the authoritative contract. Canonical root fields:
settings, assets, tracks, clips, view. No root version or transitions.
Settings: width,height,frame_rate:{numerator,denominator},audio_sample_rate.
Assets: id (ULID),kind (Video/Image/Audio),path,name,duration,width,height,framerate,
frame_rate_numerator,frame_rate_denominator,codec,has_audio.
Tracks: id,name,kind (Video/Audio/Text),locked,muted,visible.
Clips: {kind:Video|Audio|Text,data:{...}}.
Media data: id,track_id,asset_id,timeline_start,source_in,source_out,
video_properties:{position_x,position_y,scale},audio_properties:{gain_db,muted}.
Images are Video clips with Image assets; their source range specifies duration.
Text data: id,track_id,timeline_start,length:{secs,nanos},
properties:{text,font,font_size,color,position_x,position_y}.

Positions and media source bounds are integer frames at the timeline rate.
Ranges are end-exclusive. Video position is a pixel offset from center; scale 1
fits inside the project frame. Text position is normalized. Color is packed ARGB.
Earlier video tracks appear above later ones; text tracks appear above video.
Hidden video may still contribute audio. Muting controls audio; locking does not
affect export. View state is serialized but does not affect CLI rendering.

Legacy CLI documents using version/type/transitions are rejected with
legacy_cli_format. Do not emit the old CLI format. SRT import and automatic
silence/camera decisions are not implemented.
Use assemble for explicit agent-supplied cuts and camera choices.

Time arguments: 12.5,12.5s,375f,00:00:12.500. Rounded to the nearest frame.
Only still --at accepts percentages; 100% means final frame.
H.264/HEVC: MP4/MOV. ProRes: MOV. Audio: AAC stereo. Black background.
Render --bitrate (alias --video-bitrate) accepts bits/s with k/M suffixes.
Absent --bitrate, use duration-weighted contributing visible source video bitrate;
fallback to preset. ProRes remains profile-controlled.
New refuses existing files. Render/still require --overwrite to replace outputs.
Outputs cannot overwrite source assets. Render embeds the input document in
opencut.timeline metadata unless --no-metadata is supplied.

Exit codes: 0 success,2 usage,3 validation,4 media,5 rendering/transcription,6 I/O.
JSON errors: {error:{code,pointer,message,file,line}}. Validate returns findings.

Podcast authoring (no model calls inside OpenCut):
  opencut schema --kind recipe --json
  opencut --project-root /project assemble recipe.json --dry-run --json
  opencut --project-root /project assemble recipe.json -o episode.timeline.json --json
Recipe: settings, time_base:{numerator,denominator} (seconds/tick), sources:
[{name,path,source_offset}], master_audio (source name), gain_db (optional, default 0),
retained:[{start,end}], cameras:[{source,start,end}]. All times are integer ticks.
Master audio defines episode time and requires zero offset and an audio stream.
source_time = episode_time + source_offset. Paths resolve from --project-root.
Ranges are half-open, ordered, nonnegative, nonoverlapping, nonempty. Cameras must
cover all retained frames. Cuts ripple video and master audio together; camera
switches split only video. Camera audio is muted. Each source may have at most one
video and one audio stream. No captions or drift correction in recipes yet.
Offsets/boundaries independently round once to project frames, ties away from zero.
Report: total frames, frame_rate, interval map, clip source/output ranges, rounding.
Dry-run does not write or require -o. Existing output needs --overwrite; recipes and
source media cannot be overwritten. Reassembly does not merge manual GUI edits.

Transcription (uploads audio to MiniMax; requires MINIMAX_API_KEY):
  opencut transcribe recording.mp4 --json
  opencut transcribe recording.wav --format srt -o subtitles.srt
  opencut transcribe recording.wav --format srt --timestamp-level word --post-merge -o subtitles.srt
  opencut transcribe recording.mp4 --format verbose_json --timestamp-level word --language zh
Audio/video input: best audio stream, normalized to mono 16 kHz WAV via vendored
FFmpeg. Requires known positive duration, at most 500 seconds including timestamp
gaps; no truncation or chunking. Upload is under 50 MB. Paths use working directory.
Formats: json, verbose_json (default, speakers/timestamps), srt, vtt.
Timestamp levels: sentence (default), word; ignored for plain json.
Language: optional BCP-47 header hint; omitted means mixed-language recognition.
Model: asr-1.0, stream=false. No automatic retries or subtitle insertion.
Without -o: result on stdout; --json wraps subtitle text as a JSON string.
With -o: atomically write selected format, return {path,format}; --overwrite is
required to replace output. Input cannot be output. SRT can be imported in editor.
Rust: async cli::transcribe::transcribe(path, api_key, &options), using Tokio.
